name: First League of Serbia and Montenegro
content:
The First League of Serbia and Montenegro was the highest level of football competition in Serbia and Montenegro between 1992 and 2006. It was established after the breakup of Yugoslavia and initially operated as the First League of FR Yugoslavia, effectively continuing the tradition of the former Yugoslav top division. The league later became known as the Serbia and Montenegro Super League during its final season.

Throughout its history, the competition underwent several format changes. During the mid-1990s, the league temporarily adopted a two-group structure, dividing clubs into separate divisions with movement between them based on performance. This system was eventually abandoned, and the championship returned to a traditional single-league format. The competition featured many of the strongest clubs from the region and remained central to football in both republics.

The league ended in 2006 after Montenegro declared independence and the country dissolved. It was replaced by separate national competitions: the Serbian Super League and the Montenegrin First League. During its existence, Partizan became the most successful club with eight league titles, while Red Star Belgrade won the final championship in the 2005–06 season.

name: Serbia and Montenegro Cup
content:
The Serbia and Montenegro Cup was the national football knockout competition of Serbia and Montenegro between 1992 and 2006. It served as the continuation of the former Yugoslav Cup after the breakup of Yugoslavia and was initially known as the FR Yugoslavia Cup. In 2003, following the country's name change, the tournament was renamed the Serbia and Montenegro Cup. It was organized by the Football Association of Serbia and Montenegro.

The competition lasted for fifteen seasons and was heavily dominated by Serbian clubs. No club from Montenegro ever reached the final during the tournament’s existence. The cup format also changed over time, with finals played over two legs between 1993 and 1998 before later switching to a single-match final.

Red Star Belgrade became the most successful team in the competition’s history, winning nine titles and reaching nearly every final. The tournament ended in 2006 after Montenegro declared independence, leading to the creation of separate national cup competitions in Serbia and Montenegro.
